newsitem.title: USA: AMBAC, MBIA shares drop on Miami fears -- analysts.
newsitem.headline: AMBAC, MBIA shares drop on Miami fears -- analysts.

text.p: Shares of municipal bond insurers AMBAC Inc and MBIA Inc dropped Tuesday amid fears that Miami's fiscal crisis will hurt earnings, stock analysts said.
But the analysts reiterated buy recommendations, arguing that the risk of default is minimal and the potential threat to insurers' revenues is extremely small.

Shares of MBIA, which insures municipal bonds through its MBIA Insurance Corp unit, fell 2-1/8 to 96-1/4 and have dropped from a Dec 3 all-time high of 103-5/8. AMBAC fell Tuesday 1-1/8 to 64-1/4 from an all-time high on Dec 3 of 69.
Louise Costikyan, who covers the companies for Merrill Lynch & Co, said in an interview that the market typically overreacts temporarily when news of distressed city credits hits the market.
Miami has reported a $68 million deficit in its $275 million budget, and the state has set up an emergency board to help the city recover.

Caitlin Long, an analyst at Salomon Brothers, agreed with Costikyan that the stocks are likely to recover quickly, as investors realize the bond insurers actually are on the hook for only very small payments, and then only in the worst-case scenario of a default, which she called unlikely.

Financial Security Assurance Holdings Ltd, which has no exposure to Miami bonds, was trading up 3/8 to 31-7/8. The other major bond insurer, Financial Guaranty Insurance Co, is not publicly traded. FGIC is a unit of GE Capital Services, a subsidiary of General Electric Co.
